Nightly builds with OpenVINO, like:
master_openvino-skl-lin64: [good](http://pullrequest.opencv.org/buildbot/builders/master_openvino-skl-lin64/builds/953) / [bad](http://pullrequest.opencv.org/buildbot/builders/master_openvino-skl-lin64/builds/954)

Test: `test_person_detection_retail_0013 (test_gapi_infer.test_gapi_infer)`

relates #19707

/cc @AsyaPronina @TolyaTalamanov @dbudniko

---

Run gapi tests only:

```
OPENCV_PYTEST_FILTER=test_gapi* ./setup_vars.sh python3 <opencv_dir>/modules/python/test/test.py -v --repo <opencv_dir>
```

review_comments:
@AsyaPronina we shouldn't consider the channel size in bytes, it's reason to use `step1()`

From OpenCV documentation:
```
Returns a normalized step.

The method returns a matrix step divided by Mat::elemSize1() . It can be useful to quickly access an arbitrary matrix element.
```
looks like the original code actually is correct in terms of order for "blocked_dims", they should come in actual order NHWC..
I agree. BlockedDims already describes the physical dimensions.

BTW `{1, height, width, channels}` also works,    
 but I think  `{1, channels, height, width}` is a bit clearer, @AsyaPronina  what do you think ?
`{1, channels, height, width}` - the correct way

> `{1, channels, height, width} /* dims */`
> ...
> `{strideH * height, strideH, channels, 1} /* strides for dims */`

Does `strides` correspond to `dims` after the change?

Usually dims follow in logical order - `NCHW`, but strides describe actual layout.
The problem was in `step` we don't need to consider size of precision in bytes there.
For instance: CV_FLOAT32C3 - 3 elements in strides, but we used 3 * sizeof(float)
@ilya-lavrenov Could you please take a look how to properly pass cv::Mat to `InferenceEngine` here? (or point to some example in IE / OMZ)

https://docs.openvinotoolkit.org/latest/openvino_docs_IE_DG_Memory_primitives.html

Code after the fix looks good to me
